subject: Clarify invoice discrepancy: overhang credits & context ceiling reconciliation
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Health Billing <billing@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Discrepancy on March pilot invoice — rounding and context ceiling

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for running the pilot with us — overall the service has been great. Our finance team flagged the March invoice and asked for a quick reconciliation: the total billed for the pilot period is ~$3.2k higher than our expected run-rate. We dug into the line items and it looks like a lot of the variance comes from the per-call rounding and a "context ceiling" concept where multiple short calls appear to be billed as if they hit a higher context length.

Attached is the sample invoice and a CSV export with the call counts. Can you confirm: 1) whether you round partial token buckets up to the next billing quantum and 2) whether context ceiling (max context charged per session) is applied per call or per conversation?

We'd like to avoid surprising charges for our internal teams; if there's an overbilling we will need a credit and don't want to wait until year-end true-up. Happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

Elena
Finance Ops | Acme Health

Attachment: acme_sample_invoice_030126.pdf (pdf, 128KB)
Attachment: pilot_billing_breakdown.csv (csv, 23KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Morales <elena@acmehealth.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-29T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March pilot invoice — rounding and context ceiling

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and the attachments, very helpful. I'm looping in Karthik (sales) and Marissa (finance) to confirm and propose remediation. Quick answers up-front while we dig into the raw usage:

- Rounding: Our billing currently bins token usage into a 128-token quantum for the per-call charge when using the streaming endpoint; partial quanta are rounded up on a per-request basis.
- Context ceiling: For pilot mode we apply a conversation-level context ceiling for the active prefix (to avoid microburst charges from repeated long-history reads). That said, there are edge cases where short, repeated calls are billed as hitting the ceiling if the KV cache was cold and we re-ingested the same history.

We'll validate the specific calls in your CSV and propose either a one-time credit for obvious overhang or an amortized adjustment across the next two invoices. Marissa: can you pull the call-level trace for ACME-2026-PILOT-42 and confirm the quantum rounding math and whether cache cold-starts triggered the ceiling for the time windows Elena attached?

If preferable, I'm free for a 30-minute call this afternoon.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Tel: +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: billing_calc_sheet_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 45KB)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-03-29T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March pilot invoice — rounding and context ceiling

Thanks V — looping product / engineering mentally here but a few commercial notes:

1) For pilots we typically grant a single-month overhang credit when rounding policy produced >5% delta vs expected usage. Elena, what's your expected variance threshold?
2) If cache cold-starts are the root cause we should offer an immediate credit + a note recommending the dedicated KV warmup flag or a short TTL change to avoid recurrence.

Marissa, if you can pull the raw per-call token counts my preference is to issue a credit now rather than waiting for a true-up that extends invoice cycles. We can reconcile the accounting behind the scenes (credit memo + HubSpot note).

Karthik
Director, Sales | Redwood Inference

(added to thread for approval)

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-03-29T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March pilot invoice — rounding and context ceiling

I pulled the usage traces and reproduced the math:

- Total billed tokens (per-request quanta applied): 1,142,432 tokens -> billed as 1,153,152 tokens after 128-token up-rounding across N requests. That rounding added ~10,240 tokens to the invoice (~$1,280 at the pilot unit rate).
- Context ceiling hits: there were three sessions where the KV cache miss forced a replay of ~9k tokens each; product recorded them as active-history reads and we billed them under the 16k context-ceiling slab. That accounts for the remaining ~1.9k of the gap once we apply unit price.

Proposal: issue a one-time credit of $3,200 (covers the rounded quanta + the three ceiling replays). We will create Credit Memo CM-ACME-0326 and apply it to the April invoice. Accounting prefers applying the credit to the next invoice (keeps AR clean) but is ok to issue an immediate refund if Acme insists.

Notes for product: we should flag that the current pilot defaults to 128-token quanta; if we offer customers a 64-token quantum for specific pilots the rounding delta reduces materially. Also recommend we expose the cache-warm flag in the pilot quickstart.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: calculation_walkthrough.md (txt, 8KB)

From: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>

Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, billing@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: Discrepancy on March pilot invoice — rounding and context ceiling

Hi Elena — thanks for your patience. We reviewed the traces and we're proposing the following to make this right: 

1) One-time credit of $3,200 (Credit Memo CM-ACME-0326) to be applied to your April invoice. If you prefer an immediate refund let me know and I'll escalate to finance.
2) Technical mitigation: we'll enable an optional 64-token billing quantum for your pilot environment and provide an ops note on using the KV warmup flag to prevent the three replay events that triggered the context ceiling billing.

If that sounds acceptable I'll have Marissa generate the credit memo and Karthik will confirm commercial language. We can also schedule a 20-minute technical walkthrough for your devs to show the warmup flow.

Thanks again — looking forward to continuing the pilot.

Best,
Vanessa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
